title: An array and its length
description:
When a C-style array is passed to a function it "decays" into a pointer to its first element and forgets its size, so the length has to be passed separately.

Write `int sumArray(const int* data, std::size_t length)`.

Then write the modern version, `int sumSpan(std::span<const int> data)`. A `std::span` carries the pointer and the length together, and works with C arrays, `std::array` and `std::vector` alike.
hints: `sumArray` is an ordinary index loop from 0 to `length`, reading `data[i]`.
`sumSpan` needs no length parameter: a range-based loop, `for (int value : data)`, walks the span directly.
